title: Trace-formula orbit weights arise from graph-diagonal geometry
claim: The Selberg calculation and the coordinate-free flow calculation expose the same concrete source of periodic-orbit weights: restricting a propagator kernel from a flow graph to the diagonal produces a Jacobian, expressed for a closed orbit through the inverse determinant of one minus its Poincare return map. In the hyperbolic quotient this becomes the primitive-length, repetition, and stability weight in the smoothed Selberg trace formula; a resulting wave-trace singularity can then force a lower bound on averaged spectral-counting fluctuation.
historical_or_program_relation: The sequence runs from an exact hyperbolic image-sum computation, through a coordinate-free explanation of why the determinant is generated rather than inserted, to using the trace singularity as a quantitative witness in a Weyl-remainder problem.
limits: The cited Selberg formula has restricted conjugacy types and test-function hypotheses, the general flow derivation requires graph-diagonal transversality, and the Weyl-remainder consequence is an averaged bound. None supplies a zeta Hamiltonian or identifies Riemann zeros as a self-adjoint spectrum.

title: Extending zero-correlation bandwidth forces shifted-prime input
claim: A Fourier test function converts information about the transform F(alpha) into selected zero-difference statistics, but diagonal Parseval control lasts only while the associated prime Dirichlet polynomial is shorter than the averaging interval. Passing the alpha=1 boundary exposes the off-diagonal sums of shifted von Mangoldt values; an independent near-diagonal phase analysis reaches the same shifted mean after prime powers are compressed into Lambda(n). Thus the missing arithmetic object is not generic better error control but translation correlation of prime-power weights.
historical_or_program_relation: Montgomery's support-limited theorem identifies the exact boundary where diagonalization ceases to suffice, while the later quantum-chaos derivation reobtains the same shifted-prime statistic from the oscillatory spectral-density expansion.
limits: Both routes use smoothing, and the later route additionally uses a small-shift expansion and replaces a fluctuating product by an unresolved mean. Agreement on the bottleneck does not prove Hardy-Littlewood estimates, full pair correlation, or RH.

title: Local trace identities do not assemble without a global normalization law
claim: Cutoff kernel summation can reduce an S-local or one-place scaling trace to explicit principal-value terms, with logarithmic differentiation turning multiplicative scaling into additive local contributions. The remaining Weil-positivity program is nevertheless globally coupled: principal-value constants at different places must be coordinated, and the proposed coordinator is the global Poisson formula rather than an arbitrary collection of locally valid normalizations.
historical_or_program_relation: The 1999 S-local trace proof supplies controlled local terms; the 2019 scaling-Hamiltonian program preserves those canonical local constructions while identifying compatible global normalization as the unresolved boundary between the analytic trace route and a global geometric interpretation.
limits: The local trace formulas and tail estimates do not establish global Weil positivity. The Poisson-coordination step is programmatic here, normalization is explicitly error-sensitive, and the geometric route supplies interpretation rather than a completed proof.

title: Prolate modes replace impossible exact localization by an ordered spectral approximation
claim: At the Archimedean place, simultaneous exact compact support in a variable and its Fourier dual is impossible, so the function-field-style intersection is replaced by a concentration problem. Prolate spheroidal modes diagonalize the product of the two projections and sharply order the near-intersection; scaling-compatible Fourier self-duality also feeds concrete Sonine functions into this setting. A later self-adjoint prolate extension and Dirac square root use that ordered localization to reproduce the Archimedean high-energy term in the zeta-zero counting law.
historical_or_program_relation: The program evolves from repairing a failed exact-support transplant, through an explicit self-dual Sonine construction, to a self-adjoint ultraviolet model whose target is the coarse Archimedean counting invariant.
limits: Controlled concentration is not exact common support, and matching a high-energy counting law is much weaker than reproducing individual zeros, their oscillations, or the prime terms of an explicit formula. The cited stages do not prove RH.

title: A Hilbert-Polya model must constrain zeros rather than install them
claim: The naturalness requirement and the survey-level Hilbert-Polya implication combine into an operational audit: construct the space, operator, domain, and adjoint independently; prove a complete correspondence with all nontrivial zeros; only then use self-adjointness to force real spectral parameters. Theta-weighted pairings and difference-operator inverses show why this ordering matters: their chosen kernels already generate completed-zeta or Hurwitz-zeta values, while non-self-adjointness, an abstract zeta-valued replacement for a scalar product, inverse-kernel ambiguity, and missing domain control leave no independent spectral constraint.
historical_or_program_relation: The general Hilbert-Polya motivation is sharpened by later constructions that make answer-encoding diagnosable at the precise kernel, inverse, inner-product, and domain stages.
limits: Encoding zeta in a kernel or boundary condition is not by itself a refutation; such a construction could still become explanatory if its choices are independently canonical and its operator theory is completed. The cited models do not currently establish those conditions or a no-go theorem.

title: Reflection symmetries organize spectral labels without forcing reality
claim: Poisson-derived functional-equation reflection explains the zeta zero set's symmetric orbits, and affine label maps render a hypothetical off-line orbit as a rectangle; neither operation fixes each point on the critical line. Modified PT symmetry has the analogous limitation on an operator spectrum: it enforces paired labels or complex-conjugate eigenvalues but does not supply self-adjointness or the required reality pattern. Continuous parameter-independence could turn discreteness into fixed-point rigidity, but only if that invariance is independently proved.
historical_or_program_relation: Analytic reflection is repeatedly imported into spectral language; the later operator proposals reveal that setwise invariance must be supplemented by a genuine rigidity mechanism before it can bear the RH conclusion.
limits: The functional equation, affine-label family, and modified PT action are distinct symmetries on distinct spaces. The parameter-independence premise is RH-equivalent in the cited construction, and no source here proves it or derives spectral reality from symmetry alone.

title: The boundary condition is the quantization hinge, not a finishing detail
claim: Concrete boundary models separate three levels of spectral legitimacy. A rank-two boundary trap exhibits destructive interference as an actual confinement mechanism, and half-line self-adjoint extension theory turns momentum ambiguity into cosine and sine sectors with definite gamma phases. By contrast, evaluating a formal Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunction at zero produces the desired zeta secular equation before an admissible common domain is known. The black-hole dilation program explicitly tries to close that gap by deriving a phase-space boundary identification from a finite D4 action and gauged CPT, with parity routing modes to zeta or Dirichlet-beta conditions.
historical_or_program_relation: The research burden shifts from choosing a boundary that reproduces zeros to deriving a boundary or extension from independent symmetry and domain principles that also survive time evolution.
limits: The trapping and half-line examples do not themselves realize the Riemann spectrum. The Hurwitz-zeta construction remains formal, while gauged CPT, the physical quotient, completeness, and stability of the black-hole model are assumptions or open problems rather than validated boundary selection.

title: The same dilation flow supports counted-level and missing-level readings
claim: For the xp dilation flow, phase-space regularization is semantically active. Lower cutoffs yield the smooth Riemann term as present, emission-like levels, while a bounding box yields a divergent continuum count minus that term and hence a missing-state or absorption reading. A symplectic cutoff comparison preserves area and the leading count across coordinates, but phase, boundary data, regulator-dependent linear terms, discreteness, and the oscillatory zero contribution are not preserved by that coarse invariant.
historical_or_program_relation: Berry-Keating and Connes-style constructions are best compared by holding the bulk dilation dynamics fixed and varying the regulated region; later exact finite-model comparisons isolate which asymptotic terms survive and which remember the cutoff.
limits: The constructions are not isospectral realizations of one established operator, and agreement of leading Weyl terms does not choose between emission and absorption. None of the cited counts supplies the missing boundary conditions or explains the individual Riemann zeros.

title: Prescribed spectral wiggles require an independent law to become explanatory
claim: Matching the smooth zero staircase leaves the arithmetic oscillation problem untouched. One inverse construction can map a desired density fluctuation into a wiggly phase-space boundary and then into localized waves whose shapes differ with exact-zero phase data, showing concretely where fine spectral information can reside. Conversely, tested inverse-spectrum perturbations and prime-indexed level deletions produce smooth multi-scale arctangent responses and fail to reproduce the irregular zero count. The comparison makes independent generation of the boundary phase, not its post hoc reconstruction, the explanatory test.
historical_or_program_relation: After semiclassical xp counting established the coarse law, later programs split into inverse boundary encoding and attempts to generate fluctuations through modified levels; their contrast distinguishes representational capacity from a predictive spectral mechanism.
limits: The inverse boundary is constructed from the target fluctuation and is unique only in a stated monotone regime, so it risks answer-encoding. The failed perturbation and deletion experiments concern particular inverse models and do not constitute a no-go theorem for all bulk or boundary dynamics.

title: Random-matrix symmetry belongs to a family and an operator, not to arithmetic in general
claim: The sine-kernel determinant supplies a candidate hierarchy for zeta zero statistics, while characteristic-polynomial moments isolate a universal ensemble factor only after source-specific arithmetic factors are removed. Katz-Sarnak sharpens the comparison by making the arithmetic family determine the compact symmetry type. Arithmetic quantum chaos adds an operator-level correction: when Laplace spectra violate a generic random-matrix prediction, Hecke spectra generated by the same arithmetic structure may be the observables that carry the relevant random-matrix law.
historical_or_program_relation: The analogy develops from a single-spectrum spacing conjecture, through factorized moment predictions and family-dependent symmetry, to reassignment of the statistical model from the geometric Hamiltonian to commuting arithmetic operators.
limits: The finite-field family model is the proved case cited here; number-field and zeta predictions remain asymptotic or conjectural. Ensemble agreement neither constructs a Hilbert-Polya operator nor proves RH, and finite-height zero data may converge slowly.

title: Hidden arithmetic structure is both a universality obstruction and a spectral instrument
claim: Bounds across number-field embeddings compress allowable traces into a lattice-like tube; after the trace-length map this compression can produce large periodic-orbit multiplicities and exceptional spectral statistics. The same arithmeticity supplies an infinite commensurator and commuting nonlocal Hecke correspondences, which preserve Laplace energy while adding labels and identities useful for individual eigenfunction questions. Thus the structure that spoils a generic chaos model can simultaneously create stronger proof probes.
historical_or_program_relation: Arithmetic quantum-chaos work moves from diagnosing excess length degeneracy to exploiting the corresponding nonlocal arithmetic symmetries, replacing a simple universal-statistics expectation by an obstruction-and-instrument account.
limits: The multiplicity asymptotics and the critical exponent discussion include compressed assumptions, and subcritical degeneracy only removes a diagonal contradiction rather than proving GOE. The Hecke mechanism is specific to arithmetic quotients and is not identified here with a zeta-zero operator.

title: Phase conventions can import the zero count a spectral equation claims to recover
claim: Turning a phase expression into a labeled critical-line zero equation gains more than an aggregate staircase only if existence, branch choice, monotonicity, and uniqueness are established independently for every label. The proposed saturation argument compares the resulting critical-line count with the whole-strip count, while a separate branch audit shows that the integer correction to a principal argument can already contain the global staircase N(T) and then cancel the apparent arithmetic phase. This makes dependency tracing essential: count equality cannot validate the premise if the same count entered the phase convention or monotonicity claim.
historical_or_program_relation: Computational phase formulas sharpen the localization of known zeros, but later auditing relocates the proof burden from numerical root finding to global uniqueness and branch bookkeeping independent of the target count.
limits: This does not invalidate phase-based numerical localization or prove that every phase equation is circular. It applies to the cited dependency chain and branch convention; the authors themselves disclaim a rigorous saturation proof.

title: Symmetry-preserving quantization can leave a continuum of unconstrained modes
claim: The Hilbert-Polya target requires a natural operator with a discrete, complete spectral correspondence, but two Lie-Noether quantizations reduce their symmetry-preserving PDEs only to fixed temporal modes multiplied by arbitrary functions of a scaling coordinate. The reductions therefore show exactly what the selected classical symmetries determine and what they leave continuous. This aligns with the separate domain audit: discreteness cannot be inferred from a formal Hamiltonian or symmetry algebra without boundary conditions, admissible state space, adjoint, and completeness.
historical_or_program_relation: Later variational and formal-operator proposals make the old Hilbert-Polya requirement more precise by exhibiting residual functional freedom that only additional global or domain data could remove.
limits: The conclusion concerns the displayed symmetry prescriptions, not all quantizations of the classical Hamiltonian; extra boundary data could discretize the remaining amplitudes. It is a diagnosis of an unmet step, not a proof that no self-adjoint realization exists.
